title: Measuring how AI agents handle everyday wet-lab science
headline: OpenAI introduces BioBasicsBench to measure wet-lab AI agent analysis
summary: OpenAI has introduced BioBasicsBench, a new benchmark developed with Ligo to measure how well AI agents handle routine wet-lab analysis, including raw experimental data and troubleshooting. The benchmark tests 100 tasks across five areas of wet-lab work, such as protein methods and molecular cloning. Evaluations at the high reasoning-effort setting showed GPT-6 Astra earning an average of 66.7% of available credit compared to 43.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol. The release aims to track capabilities that have implications for biosafety and biosecurity.
why_it_matters: Tracking these capabilities helps organisations and developers understand the implications of advanced AI reasoning for biosafety and biosecurity as models take on complex scientific tasks.

quotes.text: That’s why we’re introducing BioBasicsBench, a new benchmark developed with Ligo, a biotech company focused on enzyme design, to measure how well agents handle routine wet-lab analysis.
Tracking these capabilities will also help us understand their implications for biosafety and biosecurity.

classification.significance_reason: The release of a specialised benchmark for wet-lab biology provides valuable evaluation methods for assessing frontier model capabilities and biosecurity risks.
